correctness.rationale: A standard-library verifier independently rebuilds the 24 \(D_4\) roots, exact squared distance classes, all 1584 faces at distance two, and checks each of 736 removals as a unique free codimension-one pair; the remainder is the exact 112-face complex with 10 vertices and 23 tetrahedra. Its vertex-2 link is the boundary of an octahedron and the vertex deletion has an explicitly replayed pure 15-tetrahedron 3-ball shelling with precisely that boundary, additionally collapsing in 42 elementary pairs. Gluing a cone on the boundary 2-sphere to the shellable 3-ball yields a PL \(3\)-sphere, and elementary collapses preserve simple-homotopy type. Computed certificate and checker were executed from actual final-package paths with VERIFY_OK.

originality.rationale: The main theorem is an explicit 736-pair elementary simplicial collapse of the 24-cell Euclidean Rips complex at radius two to a ten-vertex PL \(3\)-sphere with a checked 15-tetrahedron ball shelling, not the already published \(H_3\cong\mathbb Z\) or persistence table. The 2023 thesis gives those homology ranks but expressly places homotopy classification of 4-polytopes among further questions. A 2023 paper calls the four-dimensional cases easy without stating the explicit collapse theorem. value.rationale: The 24-cell is the canonical exceptional regular four-polytope; its Rips homology at the second Euclidean distance level was published, but the actual homotopy type and explicit small triangulated sphere model are not consequences of that calculation. A 736-elementary-collapse finite certificate, exact 10-vertex sphere and reproducible shellable 3-ball decomposition provide a natural structural strengthening of an explicit homotopy-classification gap in the literature. It is not presented as a new barcode, generic computation or minimal collapse count.
